To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the covariance of a (sub)Gaussians distribution can be estimated privately without the need to first estimate the mean, and (2) the covariance can be used to improve the sample complexity of mean estimation in a differentially private setting.

(a) we provide a new private mechanism for mean estimation that is sample efficient in the number of dimensions, and (b) we show that the private covariance matrix can be avoided in the analysis of the mechanism, which is the first result of this type

(i) we give an algorithm for private mean estimation in subgaussian distributions that achieves a sample complexity of $O(d/\alpha^2)$ and a running time of $O(d^3/\alpha^2 + d^4)$; and (ii) we give an alternative algorithm that achieves the same sample complexity, but with a running time of only $O(d^2/\alpha^2)$.
